title: GfK/NIQ UK Consumer Confidence Barometer — September 2026 (00:01 London / 19:01 ET prior day) — the survey half of the survey-versus-till disagreement
source: EST: nielseniq.com/global/en/news-center/2026/headline-score-up-three-points-to-14-in-august/, fetched direct 2026-09-15 (HTTP 200) — the August-2026 barometer release (published 2026-08-21, fieldwork 30 July to 12 August 2026, 2,000 UK respondents aged 16+) carries a publication-schedule note listing the remaining 2026 press-release dates verbatim as 'September 25th, October 23rd, November 20th and December 18th'. The 2026-09-25 date is read off that list, which is the publisher's own page. Release TIME is not read off this page and is carried as the barometer's standing convention; it should be re-verified at close-out. Filed estimate on three counts: this lane may not self-confirm an event it discovered in-sweep, market-events-data.ts's confirmed-prefix taxonomy has CB: for the US Conference Board and UMICH: for Michigan and no slot for GfK/NIQ, and the schedule is a note inside a press release rather than a standing release calendar. Discovered in the adjacency sweep of the never-assessed initial research of uk-retail-sales-2026-09-18, 2026-09-15
notes: PROPOSED BY THE uk-retail-sales-2026-09-18 LANE, 2026-09-15, seven days after its own event. It earns a slot for one reason the proposer's research made concrete: this calendar tracks US consumer sentiment EIGHTEEN times over (consumer-confidence-2026-08-25 through -2027-12-22, the Conference Board series) and tracks NO UK consumer sentiment read at all, while the UK entries it does carry are all prices, labour, fiscal and volumes. That gap is not cosmetic here — the proposer's ledger turns on a measured DISAGREEMENT between the till and the survey for the same month: BRC-KPMG called August 2026 the weakest since October 2024 (total +0.7% y/y, non-food -0.8%) while this barometer printed its HIGHEST HEADLINE IN TWO YEARS (-14, up three points) with major-purchase intentions at -7, the best since December 2021. One of those two instruments is describing GB consumer volumes better than the other, and the September editions of both publish inside five weeks of each other. SECOND REASON: it is dated by its own publisher, which is exactly what the BRC-KPMG monitor is not — the 10-23 lane refused to file that monitor twice because BRC's page states only 'at least two weeks ahead of official statistics' with no schedule. This one has a published list of dates, so the refusal does not apply and filing it costs the calendar nothing it cannot verify. Expected LOW on the same measured grounds as every UK sibling: symbols [], no UK-listed name in this book, no sterling- or rates-keyed house playbook. Estimate widens caution only; nothing date-keyed may act on this.
